Farmland anomaly screening with segmentation models pre-trained on LoveDA and applied zero-shot to Mancheng District and external regions: no LoveDA (ID) test result is reported for the same models (I2).
Human-in-the-loop GeoAI-GIS workflow for cultivated-land evidence (GF-2, Mancheng District): no paired ID/OOD evaluation of the segmentation model (I2).

Rice phenology identification in germplasm plots from multi-scale UAV and satellite time series: model trained on 2024 (4 m flight height), tested within 2024 and applied directly to 2023 (6 m flight height).
WS-DINO weed segmentation: the motion-blurred dataset is a separate benchmark on which models are trained and tested; no cross-domain test of a trained model (I2).
Transfer learning to estimate war-related crop yield losses in Ukraine: EU-trained models are fine-tuned on Ukrainian data before evaluation; no source-only Ukrainian result is reported (I3).
Mid-season parcel-based crop type mapping in Quebec (Sentinel-1/2, RF, XGBoost, DL and Transformers): validation on a random 25% of AOIs 1-4 vs test on spatially separate AOIs 5-6.
Lightweight CNN variants for chilli leaf disease classification: train/validation/test splits of one dataset (E3).

Multiyear crop mapping with temporal model transfer and automated sample purification (IEEE JSTARS): cross-year transfer accuracies of RF, SVM and 1D-CNN are shown as boxplots (Figure 5); tables are not in the retrievable copy.
EfficientNet-CBAM-prototype tomato disease classification: random splits of one dataset (E3).

Hierarchical multi-scale lesion-attention network and 25 generic backbones for multi-crop leaf disease classification: internal held-out test vs zero-shot transfer to the independent MLD24 mango corpus (Bangladesh).
Tobacco-plant segmentation in karst fields from UAV RGB (DeepLabV3+, U-Net, U-Net++, UNetFormer): validation split vs a spatially independent test set.

Crop field boundary delineation with transfer learning and weak supervision: models trained in France (full or partial labels) tested in France and in India (Planet and Airbus imagery), plus fine-tuned and India-only models.
Convolutional LSTM crop area estimation: generalisation assessed on random subsets within the same municipality (E3).
SLIC super-pixels + CNNs for corn foliar disease regions: models trained and tested separately on PlantVillage and on CD&S with random splits; no cross-dataset test (E3).
Crop type mapping with temporal sample migration: target-year maps come from classifiers trained on migrated samples; no unadapted cross-year transfer result is reported (I3).

Crop classification in sample-poor regions with deep learning and transfer learning (IRDCTS): target results use representative labelled target samples for adaptation; no source-only target result (I3).
TriNet explainable remote phenotyping from UAV imagery: evaluation on splits of the same campaign; no domain-defined hold-out (E3).
Durum wheat yield prediction from multispectral indices across 30 varieties: correlations and models fitted within one trial; no domain-defined hold-out (E3).

Crop mapping in Jilin with labels derived from the historical Crop Data Layer and DNN ensembles: each target year is classified with samples transferred and filtered from historical labels; no unadapted model transfer with an ID reference (I3).
Automated crop type mapping in Jilin with historical crop labels on Google Earth Engine: classifiers retrained per year on migrated labels; no source-only cross-year result (I3).
Wheat disease classification with field and glasshouse images (CerealConv): trained and tested on a mixed field/glasshouse dataset; no domain-defined hold-out (E3).
Transforming images of lab-grown plants into field-like composites for detector training: models trained on synthetic composites and tested on real field images (E2).
UAV weed detection with high-end (Altum) and low-cost multispectral sensors: U-Nets trained and evaluated separately on each sensor's dataset; no cross-sensor test (I2).

GWHD 2020 dataset paper (sentinel; also found by citation chasing): Faster R-CNN baseline trained on European and North American sub-datasets and tested on Australia, Japan and China; baseline values are given only in supplementary figure S2.
GWHD 2021 dataset paper (sentinel): reports competition and reference results on the test domains (weighted domain accuracy) but no in-domain result for the same models (I2).

Background-bias assessment for plant disease detection (EfficientNet-B0): the shifted test sets are image-processing variants (leaf-only, background-altered) of PlantVillage images (E2).

Improved lightweight DeepLabv3+ for winter wheat extraction from GF-2 imagery: study area vs a generalisation test in Linfen City (other region); values read from the labels printed on the bars of Figure 11.
Random forest crop-type mapping in seven German states (Sentinel-1/2): reference-system accuracy vs spatially independent target systems; values digitised from Figure 6 (medians across states).

STDAN unsupervised domain adaptation for UAV crop classification in two Korean regions (six temporal, spatial and spatiotemporal cases): source baseline, DANN, STDAN and target baseline OA digitised from Figure 12.

UAV corn yield; random k-fold vs leave-one-field-out and spatial CV compared, but performance is shown as correlation coefficients (Figures 2-5), a metric outside the protocol's synthesis set; R2 is shown only for k-fold CV (Figure 6).
Irrigated cropland mapping with U-Net, PAN and DeepLabV3+ on Sentinel-2 (California): models trained on 2019 data applied to 2018, 2020 and 2021; values digitised from Figure 8.

Summer-crop mapping (S1/S2, Dijon/Tarbes, 2020/2021): Figure 14 gives per-crop F1 for spatial, temporal and spatiotemporal transfer only; the matching within-site, within-year F1 is not reported as a value.

Stem rust hyperspectral classification, wheat -> barley: barley test F1 per model and feature space shown as boxplots (Figure 11); the matching wheat validation F1 per configuration is only shown averaged across configurations (Figure 9).

Irrigated vs rainfed cropland mapping from AlphaEarth embeddings with five classifiers: within-year accuracy in the Guanzhong Plain (2022, Table A2) vs application to 2023 and 2024 and to Kansas; transfer values digitised from Figures 10 and 12.

Early crop identification in the Hetao Irrigation District from Sentinel-1/2 with random forest: 2021 hold-out F1 per crop at its earliest identification time vs the 2021 model applied to all 2022 samples (Figure 7).
Multi-temporal crop-type mapping (Landsat + IACS) with single-year and multi-year random forests: Figures 6-7 report only independent-year accuracies; no same-year test of the same models (I2).

Soybean maturity (R8) prediction from UAV images with random forest: the in-environment test (Table 2) is for a 2018 model, while the independent-environment predictions (Figure 8) come from models trained on 2019 or 2018+2019 data; no ID result exists for the transferred models (I2).
Tomato and stem detection in greenhouses (generalisation study): models trained on perpendicular (PC) or angled (AC) camera views tested on both views with 5-fold CV; values digitised from Figure 4a.

attTFBS rice mapping from Sentinel-1 trained in the Mississippi Alluvial Plain (10-fold CV, 2019) and transferred to Northeast China: zero-shot F-score 0.2253 and 0.8816 after fine-tuning with 10 target samples (text); ID F-score digitised from Figure 5c.

Rice SPAD from UAV multispectral spectral and textural features with random forest: test split of the 2021 experiments vs an independent 2022 experiment on another field (values printed on Figures 9 and 10).

Potato yield in Mexico at municipal level (RF, SVMs, GLM): bootstrap validation on 2004-2016 (Table 3) vs the independent 2017-2018 test, shown only as a scatter plot without summary statistics (Figure 5).

Potato LCC, LAI and AGB estimation with a multi-task MMOE model (PROSAIL pre-training, few-shot meta-learning on field data): 2022 validation vs application of the 2022 model to 2021 field data (Figure 15).

Corn silage yield from PlanetScope, topography and climate (Extra Trees, Random Forest, XGBoost) on two New York dairy farms: same-field held-out test vs a neighbouring unseen field (farm-wise fit, Figure 4) and vs unseen years (year-wise fit, Figure 6). ID RMSE printed in Figure 3a; OOD values digitised from bar heights except three given in the text.

Corn/soybean semantic segmentation from Sentinel-2 (SegNet, UNet, UNet++, attention A2SegNet) with CDL labels in Iowa/Minnesota: same-year test (Table 3) vs models applied to the other two years' test sets, whose study-area boxes also differ (Figure 13; values printed on the bars). Target-year models give oracle values.

Soybean plant height and first pod insertion height from UAV vegetation indices (MLR, RF, MLP, XGBoost), 32 genotypes over three seasons: random genotype-season hold-out with all seasons in training (method 3) vs leave-one-season-out (method 2). Values only in Figure 3; method 1 is an in-sample fit and was not used.

CNN identification of SBR-transmitting planthoppers on sticky traps: the in-domain test is per-insect classification (accuracy, precision, recall, F1 on the internal held-out set), while the secondary-source traps from Giessen are evaluated only as count agreement with experts (R2, RMSE, regression slope; Figure 9). No same-metric ID-OOD pair (I2).

Cotton lint yield from Sentinel-2 monthly NDVI or four bands (MLR, bagged trees, GPR, CNN-LSTM) at four resolutions: 80/20 split of 2024 (Table 4) vs the same models on independent years 2022-2023 (Fig. 4, values printed on the bars). The field-scale independent-year table (Table 5) has no matching ID result and was not used.

Cropland mapping in Maine from AlphaEarth annual embeddings with CDL labels: random forests trained on each year 2018-2023 and evaluated on every year's held-out test patches (Figure 8 matrix, values printed; diagonal also given in text). Same patch locations each year, so the shift is temporal only.

Slovenia -> Serbia crop mapping with RF and a transformer on S1, S2 and S1+S2: source test (SLO->SLO, grey rows), naive transfer, target from-scratch and transfer learning, all in Table 5 (read from the PDF text layer).

LULC (incl. cropland and fallow land) classification with SVM-RBF, RF and CART in GEE: models trained over Uttar Pradesh in 2018 and applied to UP and Bihar in 2018, 2009 and 1998 (Tables 6-7; Table 8 is the mean of the two). Generic LULC classes; overall accuracy covers all seven classes.

PEFT of TSViT for winter-wheat segmentation: Beqaa-Lebanon models are trained on 2016-2019 and tested on 2020 only, and Munich 480 results (Table 3) are fine-tuned or from-scratch on the target; no source-only transfer is reported, so there is no ID-OOD pair (I2).

Crop-type mapping transfer between French departments (Occitanie, 11 training departments) and Kenyan regions (3) with LDA and random forest: unadjusted transfer vs oracle (within-region CV on the test regions) and the unsupervised FPSA adjustment; no source-region accuracy reported, so oracle-referenced only. Values digitised from Figures 6 and 9.

Wheat head detection on the Global Wheat Detection data (Chinese-language article): baseline YOLOv5x and EfficientDet-D5 on the local 8:2 validation split of the European/Canadian training images vs the public leaderboard of images from Australia, Japan and China (Tables 1-2, read from the PDF text layer). TTA, WBF and pseudo-label rows were not used.

Soybean maturity date from UAV imagery: model pre-trained on 2018-2019 trials (random split) and tested on the unseen 2020 trial before and after fine-tuning (Figure 3 prints the RMSE for each flight; Table 2 gives the fine-tuning ratios).
